articles.title: Gritt Robotics brings AI-assisted robotics to bolster shrinking solar workforce
articles.summary:
Robots are most effective in laboratories or controlled environments, such as a factory floor. When robots are required to automate tasks outdoors, the range of applications narrows with the number variables encountered. For this reason, construction sites remain labor-intensive locations resistant to robotics.

Solar construction sites may admit more automation than other sorts because of the regularity and essentially two-dimensional aspect of their layouts. Placement of heavy bases and even tracker tubes have been automated to some degree on many utility-scale solar projects for years. A key goal of these implementations is to have robots take over the more arduous tasks of materials transport and repetitive placement in all weather conditions.

articles.title: Africa Via, AXIAN, PIDG and FMO Sign EUR 50 Million Financing Agreement for the Kong Solaire Project
articles.summary:
Kong Solaire SAS, a project company owned by Africa Via, Axian and the Private Infrastructure Development Group (PIDG) through InfraCo, its project development solution, has signed a financing agreement with FMO, the Dutch entrepreneurial development bank, for the Kong solar photovoltaic power plant in Côte d’Ivoire.

FMO is providing the project’s entire long-term financing, amounting to up to EUR 55.5 million, with a 20-year tenor. The financing incorporates adaptations to conventional project finance structures to reflect the specific context of emerging markets in West Africa, developed jointly by the parties.

articles.title: Africa has seen oil shocks before. Why 2026 could be the turning point for clean energy
articles.summary:
Africa has been here before. Oil climbs above $100, import bills balloon, Finance ministers across the continent convene emergency sessions, and somewhere in a development bank boardroom, a clean energy investment pipeline gets quietly deprioritised while everyone waits for the price to come back down.

In 2008, the global financial crisis interrupted a Brent spike that had touched $147. articles.summary:
